results.title: Cross-lingual Cross-temporal Summarization: Dataset ...
results.content: We (1) build the first CLCTS corpus with 328 instances for hDe-En (extended version with 455 instances) and 289 for hEn-De (extended version with 501 instances), leveraging historical fiction texts and Wikipedia summaries in English and German; (2) examine the effectiveness of popular transformer end-to-end models with different intermediate fine-tuning tasks; (3) explore the potential of GPT-3.5 as a summarizer; and (4) report evaluations from humans, GPT-4, and several recent automatic evaluation metrics. Model designs include (1) corpus-based lexical substitution as an effective component for normalization systems (Rayson, Archer, and Smith 2005; Baron and Rayson 2008; Bollmann 2012); (2) rule-based models, such as phonological rules (Porta, Sancho, and Gómez 2013) and edit distance measures (Adesam, Ahlberg, and Bouma 2012; Bollmann 2012); (3) statistical models which aim to maximize the probability of contemporary word form given its historical form (Pettersson 2016); and (4) neural network (NN) models which utilize NN architectures such as encoder-decoder LSTMs (Bollmann, Bingel, and Søgaard 2017; Robertson and Goldwater 2018) or RNNs (Makarov and Clematide 2020).
